knowledge_gaps: Two distinct item IDs do not guarantee independent support: causal contextual states share history, so one influential interaction can affect both selected states. Averaging the top two affinities also permits one strong match to compensate for weak or negative second support.

The cosine support is bounded, but softplus(a) is unbounded. Its initial value is approximately 0.049, potentially negligible beside baseline logits. Gate scaling, regularization, and dataset-specific versus shared parameters need specification.

The proposed ablations do not isolate the claimed two-support mechanism. Compare baseline, top-one support, top-two average, and a second-highest-affinity residual that directly tests requiring two strong matches.

Reproduction details remain incomplete: padding exclusion, all-masked top-k handling, gradient flow, tensor shapes, checkpoint scheduling, and a concrete allocation of the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget.

Originality and difficulty ratings are optimistic without closer comparison to established candidate-conditioned history aggregation. Efficient causal deduplication, training memory, predictor consistency, and full-catalog scoring make the change more involved than adding one scalar.

With 200 validation users per category, small improvements may reflect sampling variation or repeated checkpoint selection. The report lacks paired uncertainty estimates and a predefined validation-selection schedule. Simulator feedback from twenty users cannot establish general relevance improvements.
